haiku-low.q1: Reports above 10,000 rows (by reports.row_count) take the job path; 10,000 or fewer return the CSV directly. Direct users get the CSV in the response. Job users get 202 and an emailed 24-hour link.
haiku-low.q2: No second export starts. The partial unique index blocks it and the API returns the existing record, so the page shows that export's state. A queued record with no job_id older than 5 minutes is marked failed first.
haiku-low.q3: The link works for 24 hours (86,400 seconds). The bucket deletes the file after 7 days. There is no cleanup job.
haiku-low.q4: Up to 3 attempts, waiting 60 s then 300 s. After the last failure, the record is set to failed, the user is emailed that it failed, and the page shows failed.
haiku-low.q5: The read replica only, never the primary.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports record's status field. The page calls the latest-export endpoint on load and after the POST, and polls every few seconds while queued or running.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 5,000 rows at a time from the replica, appends CSV to a buffer, and uploads an 8 MB part whenever the buffer fills. Memory stays near one batch plus one part.
haiku-low.q8: A raised error calls abort_multipart, so nothing is visible. A dead worker or timeout runs no abort, and the bucket discards the upload within 24 hours. Each retry restarts from row one with a new upload.
haiku-low.q9: They are stored on the report_exports record when the POST is made. The job receives only the export_id and loads the filters and cols from that record.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) over records with status queued or running. Two simultaneous inserts cannot both succeed, so one hits the index.
haiku-low.q11: complete_multipart must have finished and the record set to done before the link is built and emailed. A redelivered job seeing done stops without rebuilding or emailing.
haiku-low.q12: Nothing is stored and no record is made. The user gets an error with no partial file and must click again.

sonnet.q1: The API reads reports.row_count (total unfiltered rows). 10,000 or fewer: the POST response is the CSV itself, built fully in memory. Above 10,000: a background job builds the file and the user gets an immediate 202 with the export record (id, status), then later an email with a 24-hour download link.
sonnet.q2: The partial unique index (one queued/running export per user and report, regardless of filters) blocks the insert. The API reads the existing record and returns it, so no second export starts and the page shows that export's state. Exception: if the existing record is queued, has no job_id and is older than 5 minutes, it is marked failed and a new one is inserted.
sonnet.q3: The link works 24 hours (signed_url ttl 86400) and goes to the user who asked. The bucket deletes the file after 7 days; there is no cleanup job.
sonnet.q4: 3 attempts in total (waits of 60 s then 300 s). After the last fails, on_final_failure sets the record to failed and emails the user that the export failed. The page shows failed, and the user can start a new export.
sonnet.q5: The read replica only (never the primary), for both the page and the export paths.
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports table's status column (queued, running, done, failed); this is the only place export state is kept. The page calls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest on load and after the POST, and polls it every few seconds while status is queued or running. Reopening later shows the stored state.
sonnet.q7: It streams: start_multipart on key {export_id}.csv, reads 5,000 rows at a time from the replica (keyset paging), appends CSV to an in-memory buffer, and uploads a part whenever the buffer reaches about 8 MB, then uploads the final short part and calls complete_multipart. Memory stays near one batch plus one part, not the whole report. (Whether it finishes within the 30-minute attempt limit is unmeasured.)
sonnet.q8: Nothing is visible at the key before complete_multipart. If the handler raises, it calls abort_multipart and re-raises. If the worker dies or hits the 30-minute limit, no abort runs, and the bucket discards the incomplete upload within 24 hours. The next attempt restarts the handler from row one (the beginning) with a new upload.
sonnet.q9: The page sends them in the POST body from its URL at click time; the API stores them as filters and cols on the report_exports record. The job payload is only {export_id}, and the handler loads the record and uses its filters and cols.
sonnet.q10: The database partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) over records with status queued or running. The second insert hits the index and the API returns the existing record.
sonnet.q11: The file must be fully built (complete_multipart done) and the record set to done before signed_url is built and the email sent. If the job is redelivered after the record is done, the handler sees done and stops. If redelivered after complete_multipart but before done (record still running), it rebuilds the file, replaces the object at the same key, then sets done. If only the email fails, it is logged and the record stays done.
sonnet.q12: The user gets an error and no partial file (the CSV is only sent once complete, including after a 60-second kill). Nothing is stored and no record is made; the user clicks again.
